chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the Ansar came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I have been tested with a great matter. I had a slave girl whom I used to have intercourse with. One day I had intercourse with her, then I went out for my need after I had performed ritual bath, and I forgot my provision (for her) at home. I returned to the house to take it, and I found my servant boy on her belly. I counted for her from that day nine months, so she gave birth to a girl.' He said to him, 'It is not appropriate for you to have intercourse with her, nor to sell her, but spend on her from your wealth as long as you are alive. Then, upon your death, instruct that she be spent from your wealth until Allah makes a way out for her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master who impregnates his slave girl with a single act of intercourse?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the specific legal status of the *Umm al-Walad* (mother of the child) when her master impregnates her through a single act, distinguishing it from continuous ownership. The ruling prohibits selling her to ensure her stability and mandates lifelong financial support from the master, reflecting the Shia emphasis on securing the welfare of the mother and child until divine decree provides their release. This case serves as a foundational precedent for the inheritance rules of the *Mula'ana* offspring discussed in the chapter.
